title: The Horse That Grazed on the Palace Roof (ES)
summary: Akbar jokingly commands Birbal to show him a horse grazing on a rooftop. Birbal arranges a spectacle that fulfills the royal whim.
full_text:
During an idle afternoon in the imperial palace, Emperor Akbar decided to tease Birbal with a nonsensical riddle:

'Birbal, travelers tell me that in certain mystical kingdoms of the north, horses graze upon the rooftops of houses! I command you: show me a horse grazing upon a roof in Agra by tomorrow noon, or admit that your wit has failed!'

The courtiers smiled, expecting Birbal to confess defeat.

The next day at noon, Akbar walked out onto the royal balcony of the Agra Fort, overlooking the sprawling city.

In a courtyard just below the palace wall stood a small, flat-roofed mud outhouse used for storing garden tools.

Upon the flat roof, Birbal had arranged several bundles of fresh, juicy green clover and sugarcane.

Standing upon a wooden ramp beside the outhouse was an ordinary donkey! But Birbal had tied a pair of tall wooden horse-ears to the donkey's bridle, draped a magnificent horse blanket over its back, and pinned a bushy horse tail to its rear!

The donkey was munched happily on the clover upon the roof!

Birbal stood on the ground below, bowed low to Akbar on the balcony, and announced:

'Behold, Your Majesty! There is the horse grazing upon the roof, exactly as you commanded!'

Akbar stared in disbelief, then laughed: 'Birbal, that is not a horse! That is merely an ordinary donkey dressed up in horse clothes!'

Birbal looked up with innocent surprise:

'Sire! If an Emperor can issue a decree demanding that a horse graze on a rooftop like a bird, then surely an ordinary donkey has every right to believe it is an imperial warhorse!'

The entire court erupted in laughter. Akbar shook his head in fond amusement: 'You turn every absurd challenge back upon me, Birbal!' Akbar rewarded him with a purse of gold for his playful genius.
